title: Why does your brain make you procrastinate?
story: Your Brain Is Cooked, Not Lazy (saved story 6e7b6bf0, published as Procrastination Isn't Laziness, It's Dodging a Feeling)

sources.supports: Tim Pychyl and Fuschia Sirois describe procrastination as a problem of managing mood, not managing time (saved Brainrot script, researcher attribution only).
Present bias: relief in seconds feels more real than a reward next week (saved script, general account).

2018 German brain-imaging study: chronic procrastinators tended to have a larger amygdala and weaker links to a region that turns feelings into action. A correlation, not a diagnosis (saved script wording).
Dread is often worse than the task and starting often quiets the alarm (saved script; stated as 'often', not a measured result). The chart is schematic and labelled illustrative.
One study found students who forgave themselves for procrastinating before a first exam procrastinated less before the next (saved script wording).
